title: Why do I only see twelve tools?
goal: {{lena}} at {{vocab.org}} connects an assistant to PingOne's hosted MCP server and expects the full admin tool set. She sees a short list.
obstacle: The tool list is gated by the admin roles of the identity that connects. A short list looks like a broken server, so people debug the wrong thing.
control: {{mark}} checks the roles on the connecting identity first. Role gating is the control: a viewer identity never sees write tools, whatever the client asks for.

steps.title: Connect as a viewer
steps.tell: In the mock demo connection pick the viewer role and press Test connection. The health card counts the tools and says in words that a short list usually means missing roles.
steps.say: The server is fine. The identity is what the server is looking at.
steps.why: Role gating is per identity, so the same server shows different tools to different callers (pingone-mcp skill).

steps.title: Read the list
steps.tell: Open Tools. Every tool the viewer sees carries a read badge. No write tool is listed, so none can be called.
steps.say: No write tool in the list means no write path, not a hidden switch.
steps.why: A tool that is not listed cannot be called: this app also refuses a call to a tool the identity does not see.

steps.title: Switch to admin
steps.tell: Switch the demo role to admin and test again. The count grows and write and destructive tools appear, each labelled with why it was classed that way.
steps.say: Same server, same URL, a bigger list. Only the roles changed.
steps.why: The fix for a short list is a role assignment in PingOne, not a retry loop.

steps.title: Check the real numbers yourself
steps.tell: On a real tenant the count depends on your roles. The skill says a fully privileged worker sees about 60 to 70 tools. That figure is not verified by this app.
steps.say: I will quote a number only when I have measured it on our tenant.
steps.why: Numbers from a document are a starting point; the owner checks listed in docs/live-checks.md settle it.

proof.happy: The viewer list contains read tools only; the admin list contains write and destructive tools as well.
proof.blocked: As a viewer, a call to a write tool is refused because the tool is not in the list.

say: A short tool list is a roles question first, a server question last.
